items.title: Excess risk beyond the first year is uncertain
items.whyItMatters: Estimates for years two to five shrink with adjustment (claims c1, c3), and the decision about long-term follow-up turns on them.
items.opportunity: Estimate hazard ratios separately for the first year and years two to five.

items.title: Comparison group determines the answer
items.whyItMatters: Population controls overstate and infection controls understate the effect (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Report both comparisons with frailty measured before the index admission.

items.title: Loss of independence is rarely measured
items.whyItMatters: Care home entry doubles in older adults (claim c5) and matters to patients more than a hazard ratio.
items.opportunity: Include care home entry as a secondary outcome from linked address data.

items.title: Older and deprived survivors carry the highest risk
items.whyItMatters: Frailty and deprivation cluster, and people living alone lose independence most.
items.opportunity: Report absolute risks by age group, deprivation quintile and living alone.

items.title: The ten-year doubling figure has no source
items.whyItMatters: Clinicians repeat it to patients, and no retrieved record supports it.
items.opportunity: Do not use it as a planning value; report what the local data show.

errorsFound: The first scan reply assigned a certainty label although the recorded search had returned no records.
The quoted ten-year doubling of cardiovascular risk matches no retrieved record.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a registry-based cohort with two comparison groups, frailty measured before admission, time-split estimates and care home entry as a secondary outcome.
summary: Five gaps; the persistence of excess risk and the comparison group are high severity.
